new_title: 'Pretty clear to me': Cats count the cost of goal review blunder

Fri, 28 Aug, 7:40 pm, Final score, Bulldogs 96, Magpies 93
live
AFL semifinal live: Fremantle vs Geelong live blog, scores and stats from Perth Stadium
Minor premier Fremantle is bidding to avoid an ignominious straight-sets exit as it takes on Geelong in a massive AFL semifinal at Perth Stadium.
Follow the live blog below, keep up to date with all the latest stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Fremantle vs Geelong live
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
Jye Amiss gets that Freo buffer straight back
The Dockers are just too big up there. Amiss had Henry in a one-on-one this time and monstered him. Treacy is doing his best work up the ground, and Voss has been dominant at times too.
The ball is moving quickly so the forwards are getting a look. Tonight, they aren't letting anyone down. Dockers by 25 with 15 to play in the second.
Shannon Neale snaps one through! Two in a row Geelong
Geelong has been pretty efficient inside 50 tonight, and they've needed to be because it hasn't been down there much. A stand rule 50 metre penalty took Geelong from half-back to full-forward, but it looked like the Dockers had the numbers.
Alex Pearce threw one away in congestion and Neale was there to take the crumbs. The big fella's snap was a beauty.
Ollie Henry sneaks one through, Cats respond
Now it's Geelong's turn to go end to end, and they have Tom Stewart to thank for denying Voss another lead up mark inside 50. From Stewart's spoil, the Cats took the ball up the wing uncontested and found Henry inside 50.
Feels like the Cats are right on the edge here. Can the Dockers put them away early?
Isaiah Dudley on the board! Freo with another fast start!
It's happening again! The Dockers take it cleanly out of the middle through Brayshaw, before Treacy and Voss win crucial one-on-ones against Stewart and O'Sullivan at half-forward.
Treacy delivers an incredible inboard kick to Dudley, who nails his set shot from 40. This is is sensational Fremantle footy.
Key Event
QT: Fremantle 6.2 (38) leads Geelong 2.1 (13)
A simply stunning start from Freo, who made good on all of their pre-match promises and have turned up with a hunger and ferocity that the Cats have not been able to match.
The Dockers have belted them at the contest and have run the Geelong defence of their legs back towards goal. It has been jarring to see so many Fremantle players in so much space inside 50, the Cats' defence so scattered and scrambled. It's starting up the field with Brayshaw and Serong and being capitalised upon by Bolton and Voss.
There's a long way to go, but on early evidence it doesn't look like the Dockers are done with this season just yet.
Ollie Wiltshire pulls one back for the Cats
Potentially an important goal with two minutes left to play in the first quarter. The Cats have been hanging on for dear life here, and stuck a couple of goal-saving tackles in the back half before getting the footy forward.
Mitch Edwards shanked a kick forward but found the chest of Wiltshire, who converted. The Cats would probably take 25 points.
Mason Cox has a goal now too!
Everything coming up Fremantle! The Dockers are winning every contest around the ball and the backline is copping a belting as a result. Cox beat Jack Henry in the one on one in the goalquare and made no mistake with the finish.
Cox looks to get stuck into Henry after the goal, but the Cat just turned his back on him. The crowd, as you can imagine, is loving every last bit of this.
Patrick Voss has two! Dockers kick ahead!
And doesn't he love it! The Dockers are finding loose men so easily whenever they transition the ball, finding back-half scores so easily. Again it goes end to end and Voss is found all by himself on the arc.
Voss runs around to nail his set shot from 50. Freo now have as many goals in this quarter as they kicked in the whole game last week. Stunning stuff.
Michael Frederick finishes off another Freo counter!
Geelong had won itself a bit of forward territory, but the Dockers are looking so dangerous when the breakaway comes. Bolton escaped out through the middle of the ground and there were players loose everywhere.
Amiss scooped the ball up one-handed, fed Freddy and let him do the rest. Dockers by 18 points with 13 minutes to play in the first.
Patrick Dangerfield! Incredible goal for the Cats!
Has there ever been a start to a final like this? Four goals in about three and a half minutes, and this one is incredible from Dangerfield.
The Dockers are applying plenty of heat around the ball but couldn't stop Blicavs, Neale and Dangerfield that time. Danger took the ball tight to the boundary line and 55m from goal, but rolled around launched one off a step straight through the middle. Boy did they need that.
Patrick Voss has one now too! Insane Freo start!
What is happening! Three goals in under three minutes from the Dockers! They have the jump on the Cats here, who are getting absolutely belted around the ball.
The Geelong defence is totally lost too, as both Voss and Amiss were alone out the back there. Clark took off from half-back and split the Cats wide open.
Shai Bolton has two already! Freo on fire!
How about this from the Dockers?! That's how you get rid of the nerves!
Two centre clearances, two goals to Shai Bolton. This one comes via a sensational finish on the run from 50 which brings the house down. Delerium in the west already.
Shai Bolton strokes home the opening goal for Freo!
Dream start for Freo! The Dockers take it out of the middle and the composure of Serong finds Bolton in space inside 50. Bolton converts and the Dockers are away.
Half the Freo team ran straight to Bailey Smith to get stuck into him, I think because he let Bolton run free.
The goal umpire then holds his arms up as an NFL referee would signal a touchdown, instead of the traditional goal signal. Which is... not for me.
Ready to go in Perth!
The Welcome to Country and national anthems have been completed, the latter's conclusion met by an almighty roar.
The players are taking their positions now with a steely purpose. Jeremy Cameron looks like he's starting on the wing, Oisin Mullin is standing next to Caleb Serong, Pat Voss is getting stuck into Tom Stewart.
Ball is in the air, let's go.
The teams have taken to the field
Tremendous wall of noise for the Freo players as they strode onto Perth Stadium for the final time this season. The Dockers fans have been on one hell of a ride this year and they certainly aren't ready for it to end just yet.
The players from both sides are going through their final run-throughs before we get to the pre-match formalities. Not long to go now at all.
Thoughts from the outer
Evening Dean . Who's your pick? As a Hawker I'll have Fremantle 'cos I always hate playing Geelong in finals !
- Phillip
Hi Dean, I thought last week that Freo has run out of puff at the wrong end of the year. I have a feeling they're going to go out in finals like Adelaide did last year. Cheers, Anni
- Anni
A couple of comments coming in from our readers.
And to answer Phillip's question, I don't normally like letting my tips into the blogs but I have seen a lot of Freo this year and never once had them down as a straight-sets team. We'll see.
What went wrong for the Dockers?
Cody Atkinson and Sean Lawson had a look into the numbers to get an idea of what let the Dockers down against Hawthorn.
When looking Fremantle's dip the biggest story is what is happening at the contest - or more importantly what isn't happening.
Fremantle's midfield and front half group is blessed with attacking talent, able to turn a half-chance into a broken line or shot at goal.
They are sometimes less able to control the ball when it hits the deck, especially when there are even numbers at the contest.
Against disciplined midfields, the Dockers have struggled to find the supply they need to churn the scoreboard over.
Check out the full piece for far more.
The vets talk it over
Patrick Dangerfield, his back to the photographer here, is fresh off the back of a five-goal elimination final against Carlton. Tom Stewart remains one of the most significant and influential defenders in the game, his absence in last year's grand final a critical blow for Geelong's chances.
So much of Freo's hopes rest on youth tonight, but Geelong on the other hand will be turning to the tried and tested.
How the teams got here
It was a chastening Thursday night for Fremantle last week. Riding into the finals series with boundless confidence after a dominant home and away season and minor premiership, the Dockers were taught a lesson by the relentless Hawks.
Too many went missing, too many failed to step up on the big stage, and overall the Hawks looked a more powerful and finals-ready unit than their rivals from the west. Freo were well beaten, never in the contest, and copped a pasting in the media for their efforts.
Geelong was challenged early by Carlton and looked in strife during periods of the first half, but after the long break flicked a switch and rather cruised to victory in their elimination final.
The best word to sum up the Cats' performance was professional. It was a "been there, done that" finals win from a side packed with experience and premiership players. They didn't panic when things weren't going well, and they didn't let up when the worm turned.
So tonight then. The Dockers will be breathing fire, certain they can't put in two stinkers in a row. This will be their last chance to play in front of their home crowd, and those fans will be just as ferocious the players.
But the Cats will look at Hawthorn last week and see a blueprint. Geelong is as well position as any of the remaining contenders to take a scalp like Freo's on the road, and might sense they are there to be taken.

Fri, 28 Aug, 7:40 pm, Final score, Bulldogs 96, Magpies 93
Fremantle defeats Geelong in AFL semifinal, as Ollie Dempsey goal controversially not awarded
Geelong coach Chris Scott has tried his best to downplay his reaction to Oliver Dempsey's controversial non-goal during Friday night's 14-point semi-final loss to Fremantle, saying sometimes he punches walls when he's happy.
Scott threw his arms up in the air in disbelief before giving the wall of the Perth Stadium coaching box a light punch when Dempsey's spectacular effort in the goalsquare was ruled to be a behind.
Instead of trying to mark Bailey Smith's rushed kick forward, Dempsey unleashed a bicycle-style kick over his shoulder while under the close attention of Matthew Johnson to volley through what looked to be a spectacular goal.
The goal umpire thought it had been touched, so it went to the AFL Review Centre for the final call.
Replays appeared to show the ball had hit Johnson's bicep before Dempsey's boot deflected the ball in, but the ARC declared the evidence wasn't sufficient, meaning the goal umpire's initial call of touch had to stand.
"I was surprised it was taking so long. It looked pretty clear to me," Scott said.
"But it's not for me to judge. From what I'm told, everyone has the same opinion that Ollie did."
When asked about his punch of the wall, Scott gave an unexpected answer.
"Sometimes I punch the wall when I'm happy. Sometimes I punch the wall when I'm annoyed," he said.
"There were a few moments where we had momentum and for one reason or another we couldn't capitalise on it. That was probably one of them.
"There's some strange things in the game at the moment that are better off being spoken about in the cold light of day, probably in November, rather than September."
Had Dempsey's effort been paid a goal, Geelong would have closed the margin to eight points early in the third quarter.
The Cats still managed to kick four of the next five goals after that incident to snatch an eight-point lead, before the Luke Jackson-inspired Dockers hit back to secure the 18.12 (120) to 16.10 (106) win and book a spot in the preliminary final against Sydney.
The Dockers are yet to win a premiership after joining the AFL in 1995.
Longmuir says Dockers have underdog status
Fremantle coach Justin Longmuir is claiming underdog status for the preliminary final against a decimated Sydney, as the odds of defender Brennan Cox fronting up appear slim.
"The job's not done," Longmuir said.
"I just spoke to the players then that it feels great, we played a really good brand of footy, you should get a lot of confidence out of that.
"But job's not done. So go 1-0 again."
Sydney are a club still reeling after suspending Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice for the rest of the season for their roles in the Pullman Hotel saga.
Captain Callum Mills is also out for the rest of the season after rupturing his ACL.
The Swans defied the odds to crush Brisbane by 53 points in last week's qualifying final, but whether they can produce another huge effort with their weakened side against Fremantle remains to be seen.
Even though the Dockers have been installed as early favourites, Longmuir was talking up his side as the underdogs given the game will be played at the SCG.
"What they did against Brisbane, clearly it didn't seem like they missed any of those players," Longmuir said.
"They played a fantastic, selfless brand of footy.
"We'll go over there as underdogs, and they'll be really confident after their win against Brisbane, and they'll be heavy favourites on their home deck.
"We'll go over there and give it our best."
Cox had been slated for a return for the preliminary final week after injuring his calf in the final-round loss to Carlton.
But with Oscar McDonald performing soundly and Cox's body having shown some worrying signs even before the calf injury, there may not be room for Cox to win back his spot.
"Even before he got injured, he hadn't been putting the string of work together, so he's going to be pushing it," Longmuir said.
"He hasn't main trained yet, but we'll see where it falls. I think the majority of players would tick their role tonight.
"So when you're in the team and you play your role, it is hard to make changes."
Look back at how the action unfolded in our live blog.

That's it from the blog tonight
One down, one to go on semifinal weekend. Freo are safely through to a prelim in Sydney next weekend, but we await tomorrow night's game to see who of Brisbane and Adelaide will play Hawthorn in the other preliminary final.
Hope to see you back here for that one tomorrow. Until then, thanks for your company this evening and goodnight.
Chris Scott is up for his press conference
The Geelong coach is speaking to the media now.
"There's a lot of emotions when you lose the last game. But I think it's appropriate to talk about our perspective initially and the way we hung in this season. This game was symptomatic of our season. A lot of things went wrong, we found ourselves behind the eight ball at times and found a way to hang in and give ourselves a chance.
"After a start like that, a lot of other teams would have turned up their toes. You go back to parts of the season where we thought "that's gonna make it really hard for us", but we hung in there."
On the Ollie Dempsey non-goal decision:
"I think the best thing to do is not reflect on it at all. I was supposed it was taking so long, it looked pretty clear to me. But it's not for me to judge.
"Post-game, especially post-loss, especially post-loss in a final, is not a time when I'm thinking clearly and not a time to litigate a decision like that. From what I'm told, everyone has the same opinion as Ollie did."
Match report: Dockers thwart Cats in pulsating semifinal
The Flagmantle dream is still alive for 2026 after ruckman Luke Jackson produced a Herculean display to lead Fremantle to a pulsating 14-point semi-final win over Geelong in Perth.
In front of 59,725 fans at Perth Stadium on Friday night, Fremantle skipped out to a 38-7 lead before Geelong hit the front in the third quarter on the back of three quick goals to Oliver Henry.
Staring down the barrel of a straight-sets finals exit, Fremantle lifted when it mattered most, with Jackson the biggest hero of them all.
Jackson kicked two late goals in the third quarter and set up another for Patrick Voss to give Fremantle back the lead.
In a pressure-filled final term, Geelong cut a 24-point deficit back to eight points with 75 seconds remaining.
But Wharfie Time - played for just the second time this year - sent the crowd into a frenzy, with Voss kicking his fourth goal from the ensuing centre clearance as Fremantle sealed the 18.12 (120) to 16.10 (106) victory.
The win set up a preliminary final against the Swans in Sydney next week.
Henry kicked a career-high five goals for Geelong, while Shannon Neale chipped in with three.
Geelong had made eight preliminary finals in the past 10 seasons, but having to travel to Perth for this year's semi-final proved a bridge too far.
Bailey Smith racked up 29 disposals and 751m gained, while Patrick Dangerfield followed up his five-goal haul against Carlton with two majors and two goal assists.
Jackson (25 disposals, 35 hitouts, eight clearances, two goals) was a clear best-on-ground, while Voss's four goals were also crucial.
Shai Bolton made up for his quiet display in last week's 32-point loss to Hawthorn with two goals from 26 disposals.
AAP
Patrick Dangerfield speaks after 'bittersweet' defeat
Freo's heroes on the night
There superstars had to deliver after laying an egg last week, and they most certainly did. Let's go through a few who I thought were the Dockers' best:
Luke Jackson: 25 disposals, 35 hit outs, eight clearances, 12 score involvements, two goals
Caleb Serong: 23 disposals, six clearances, 11 contested possessions, one goal
Andy Brayshaw: 24 disposals, four clearances, four tackles
Shai Bolton: 26 disposals, four clearances, eight tackles, 10 score involvements, two goals
Key Event
FT: Fremantle 18.12 (120) def Geelong 16.10 (106)
Wow. Not entirely sure what I've just watched there, but what I can report is that Fremantle will play in a preliminary final next week against the Sydney Swans.
Honestly I thought this game was over three minutes in, such was the power of the Dockers' start to this game. I definitely thought it was over at three-quarter-time, after another five-minute burst of inspiration before the break. In truth it probably wasn't over until those final seconds, with the ball in Patrick Voss's hands and then on his boot.
I guess the Cats deserve immense credit for fighting back as they did, time and again. They never thought this game was gone at any stage, and for a while there looked like they might pull off the heist.
But it's Freo's night, as it had to be. Straight sets would have been devastating after the season they have had, but a handful of those Freo boys weren't about to let that happen. It's curtains for the Cats, but September is only just beginning for the Dockers.
Patrick Voss calls game! Fremantle wins!
Wharfie Time works again! The Dockers win the critical centre clearance, get it deep to Voss who wins the free kick and set off the greatest celebration Fremantle has seen in 13 years!
What a game. What a night for the Dockers.
Tom Stewart has kicked a goal for Geelong!
First of all, that says it all about this game really.
More importantly though, it's an eight-point game. The Cats have to kick two goals in 1:15.
And what's this? They've just declared Wharfie Time.
Five minutes to play
It's a 14-point lead currently thanks to a rushed Fremantle behind and a shocking miss from Murphy Reid.
But crucially time has come off the clock. The Cats need three goals in no time. It looks unlikely, but you can never say never tonight.
Shannon Neale kicks another for the Cats! My word!
Crazy, crazy, stupid, insane, mad, ridiculous game.
The Serong goal had ended it! Surely! Nope, the Cats have kicked two goals from centre bounce to get the margin back to 12 almost immediately.
Neale was awarded a free kick for a very slight hold from Pearce on the lead, and drilled his set shot. Still 7:36 to play. Heaps of time now.
Shaun Mannagh hits straight back for Geelong
Or not. Who knows. It's a mad, mad game.
Patrick Dangerfield is in the middle for the first time all game, and he influenced that clearance heavily. The ball emerged and Mannagh was released. His kick on goal from 50 was converted. Hope?
Caleb Serong rises to the occasion! Freo wil surely win!
It's come from a panicked, rushed clearing kick from Tom Stewart, who has not had his best evening. The ball fell on Caleb Serong's chest and the stadium fell silent.
From 50 metres out, this little champion has delivered for his club yet again. What a footballer he is.
The lead is 24 points with eight minutes and change to play. I think the Dockers are into a preliminary final.
Ollie Henry gets one back for the Cats
That's goal number five for Henry, and in the nick of time too. This one comes from a loose ball 40 from goal, which he gathered and converted with a fine left-foot snap.
Back to 17 points. Ten minutes to play. Not done yet.
Michael Frederick kicks the first of the last! Freo nearly there!
With five and a half minutes wiped off the clock, the Dockers kick the opening goal of the term through Frederick and that might just break the back of this Geelong resistance.
Johnson had a massive win on the wing over Dempsey before he found Frederick. Feels like Johnson has had a significant night.
Key Event
3QT: Fremantle 15.6 (96) leads Geelong 12.8 (80)
Not sure there's been a more manic, less predictable game this season than the one we are watching tonight.
Geelong just played the perfect third quarter, right up until its last five minutes. The Cats dominated the play, missed some chances but eventually took enough to claim the lead. Their opponents looked slow and nervous and out of ideas.
And then, in the blink of an eye, it was all wiped away. In such a manner that this may not be recoverable for Geelong. Chris Scott will say the margin is only 16 points and they still won the term, but it doesn't feel like it anymore. It feels like Freo just threw the knockout blow.
But tonight, it seems nobody really knows anything.
Luke Jackson kicks another one after the siren!
It's pandemonium! In the space of five minutes, it feels like the Dockers have won the game! The Cats are shellshocked.
It's come from another free kick, as three of those four goals have, this one conceded by Edwards in the ruck. Haven't seen a replay so not sure what happened, but it's fair to say Jackson has absolutely taken Edwards to the cleaners in these last few minutes and maybe won his team the game in the process.
Patrick Voss has kicked another one for Fremantle!
In the space of three minutes, the game has totally changed again! The Dockers lead by 10 and are going to roar into the final term with a head of steam!
That was poor by the Cats, first from Edwards getting slaughtered in the ruck again by Jackson and then by Stewart who just watched as Voss ran free into space to receive the handball and goal. The crowd is going absolutely insane now with seconds to go.
Josh Treacy puts Fremantle back in front!
Another free kick to Fremantle gets them forward out of the middle, and Serong's pass to Treacy was a scorcher.
The Big Cohuna rocks back, let's it fly and splits the middle. And just like that, Freo are back in front!
Luke Jackson pulls one back for Freo
Under three minutes to play in the third, that goal is massive for the Dockers. All momentum gone, they needed a goal more than oxygen right now.
A sloppy free kick conceded by Edwards hands Jackson a shot which he doesn't pass up. It's a gift, but Jackson held his nerve from 40 out. Big moment.

What went wrong for the Dockers? Cody Atkinson and Sean Lawson had a look into the numbers to get an idea of what let the Dockers down against Hawthorn. When looking Fremantle's dip the biggest story is what is happening at the contest - or more importantly what isn't happening. Fremantle's midfield and front half group is blessed with attacking talent, able to turn a half-chance into a broken line or shot at goal. They are sometimes less able to control the ball when it hits the deck, especially when there are even numbers at the contest. Against disciplined midfields, the Dockers have struggled to find the supply they need to churn the scoreboard over. Check out the full piece for far more. The vets talk it over Patrick Dangerfield, his back to the photographer here, is fresh off the back of a five-goal elimination final against Carlton. Tom Stewart remains one of the most significant and influential defenders in the game, his absence in last year's grand final a critical blow for Geelong's chances. So much of Freo's hopes rest on youth tonight, but Geelong on the other hand will be turning to the tried and tested. How the teams got here It was a chastening Thursday night for Fremantle last week. Riding into the finals series with boundless confidence after a dominant home and away season and minor premiership, the Dockers were taught a lesson by the relentless Hawks. Too many went missing, too many failed to step up on the big stage, and overall the Hawks looked a more powerful and finals-ready unit than their rivals from the west. Freo were well beaten, never in the contest, and copped a pasting in the media for their efforts. Geelong was challenged early by Carlton and looked in strife during periods of the first half, but after the long break flicked a switch and rather cruised to victory in their elimination final. The best word to sum up the Cats' performance was professional. It was a "been there, done that" finals win from a side packed with experience and premiership players. They didn't panic when things weren't going well, and they didn't let up when the worm turned. So tonight then. The Dockers will be breathing fire, certain they can't put in two stinkers in a row. This will be their last chance to play in front of their home crowd, and those fans will be just as ferocious the players. But the Cats will look at Hawthorn last week and see a blueprint. Geelong is as well position as any of the remaining contenders to take a scalp like Freo's on the road, and might sense they are there to be taken.
